3. On 04.03.1996, respondent No. 3 Janata Bank, Corporate Branch, Sheikh Mujib Road, Chittagong as the plaintiff instituted Mortgage Suit No. 10 of 1996 for recovery of Tk. 7,25,176/- as well as interest accrued therein till realization of the said amount impleading Md. Golam Azam as the defendant in the suit. Subsequently, the suit was renumbered as Mortgage Suit No. 17 of 1992 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Chittagong. The said suit was decreed ex-parte on 26.08.1998. The final decree was drawn up and signed on 13.06.2000. The judgment debtor having failed to pay the decretal amount the bank filed Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1999 subsequently renumbered as Artha Execution Case No. 837 of 2003 before the Artha Rin Adalat. In the execution proceeding, the mortgage property of the judgment-debtor was sold in auction on 10.01.2005 to Md. Jamal for an amount of Tk. 12,12,000/-. On 15.01.2005, the petitioner filed an application for staying all further proceedings of the execution case on the ground that the petitioner applied for waiver of interest which was under consideration of the decree-holder bank. The petitioner filed another application for staying all further proceedings of execution case, which was, rejected by the order dated 23.02.2005. Against the order dated 23.02.2005, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No.2052 of 2005 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule Nisi. The learned Judges of the High Court Division by their judgment and order dated 06.07.2006 discharged the Rule. After that, the petitioner filed an application on 26.11.2006 stating that he was willing to deposit 5% of the value of the auction sale and prayed for releasing the mortgaged property. Respondent No.4, the auction purchaser, filed an application for rejection of the application on 30.11.2006 praying for issuance of sale certificate in his favour. 

 12. We have considered the submission of the learned Advocate, the impugned judgment and the materials on record. The High Court Division came to a finding that after filing of the suit by respondents No. 3-bank, the petitioner appeared and filed a written statement but ultimately did not contest the suit and as a result, the suit was decreed ex-parte and that the judgment-debtor-petitioner did not pay the decretal amount which resulted in filing I the execution Case. The High Court Division further found that during the e8ecution proceeding the petitioner did not take any step to pay the decretal amount and that he filed writ petitions one after another to delay the matter for a long period. The High Court Division noticed that the mortgaged property was sold in auction and that sale certification was issued by the Adalat in the year 2005. The High Court Division also noticed that although the property was sold in auction in 2005, the auction purchaser could not get delivery of possession of the property till date because of the cunning devices adopted by the petitioner by filing applications and writ petitions one after another.
